title: November 21 — The Sihti line: retained residues, choosing a read, excavating delayed memory
summary: Six new reviewed projects extend the curated census 667 → 673. SihtiAI feeds spatial residue persistence into an affinity graph; SaturdayAfterRHproof isolates an action-conditioned collision; HEAD examines unsigned selective reading with supervised gradient optimization; PredictiveSihtiV2 adds a backprop-free spatial transition atlas with B-triggered routing; LazyRetrospectiveCreditAssignment tests saved-history delayed latches and a real webcam lens. The 2/20 null false latches and -31.3% webcam prediction result remain explicit. A reversible multi-stream zipper branch and a small trained diffusion comparator join the November 21 record.

nodes.claim: Exact action-dependent predictive closure witnesses: an eight-cell ring and a two-channel sum whose hidden sign matters under copy-left.
nodes.survived: A one-bit signed contrast closes the constructed action-conditioned example; a light-only ring predictor requires seven readings to synchronize for the specified task.
nodes.killed: The example does not imply arbitrary hidden histories can be recovered, and the successful candidate was offered among a deliberately small feature menu.
nodes.era: November 21: Sihti saved-residue and retrospective head

nodes.claim: Tests how a limited read head can expose an otherwise hidden contrast through selective second reads; contains supervised gradient-based training tests.
nodes.survived: Reported unsigned corrective feedback succeeded 10/10 seeds in both original and fresh controls and survived output-sign reversal; the restricted scratch reader was equivalent to positional-key attention.
nodes.killed: The training does use supervised backpropagation. No new general attention mechanism, general neural routing law or fully gradient-free training is established.
nodes.era: November 21: Sihti saved-residue and retrospective head

nodes.claim: Reuses the original lossless Sihti sieve; tests whether signed and unsigned lifetime residues can guide a second affinity graph and explores local predictive bridging.
nodes.survived: Core plus signed spatial residues reconstruct the input exactly. In a tuned synthetic stripe task, exploratory beta=8 unsigned persistence reached about 0.970 mean ARI across ten seeds while shuffled and signed controls failed.
nodes.killed: The initially proposed beta=1 setting failed. Beta=8 was selected after the stripe result, and success on that scene does not establish robust general segmentation.
nodes.era: November 21: Sihti saved-residue and retrospective head

nodes.claim: Causal local patch-based next-frame atlas using the exact Sihti split, merged motion prototypes, and local B-triggered access to additional history.
nodes.survived: Its deterministic frozen one-to-five synthetic transfer in V2.2.1 automatic mode reduced prediction MSE about 39.6% versus hold-last. The live Edge audit exercised the real browser engine and confirmed exact reconstruction.
nodes.killed: A user-supplied real-webcam run scored 480 frames and lost 31.3% to hold-last; ghost motion, slow sampling and repeated alarms remain limitations. High recalled B is not a confirmed hidden cause.
nodes.era: November 21: Sihti saved-residue and retrospective head

nodes.claim: Archives overlooked residues for later search, uses recurring predictive collisions to trigger lagged candidate excavation and sample-split statistical confirmation, and exposes real webcam residues in a visual lens.
nodes.survived: The deterministic 80-tick hidden-cue miner found exact cues in 20/20 sparse, 20/20 noisy and 20/20 polarity-reversed trials. The real-webcam retrospective probe declined to promote a weak candidate (WAIT).
nodes.killed: Two of twenty synthetic null seeds still received spurious latches: B fell but frozen held-out error worsened. The delayed-cue miner uses a simpler synthetic FastHead, not the complete spatial engine, and no real camera precursor was demonstrated.
nodes.era: November 21: Sihti saved-residue and retrospective head

nodes.claim: Explicit multi-track vector zipper prototype retains separate original vector tapes and reversible index links. Jam, slip, lock and detach decisions maintain local phase binding; Experiment 002 compares a new zipper-inspired, gated object tracker with a genuinely trained conditional pixel diffusion model on synthetic occluded videos.
nodes.survived: Original 40-seed synthetic 4D switchyard scored about 91.66% correct joins versus 91.31% for local greedy and 62.47% for fixed alignment at noise 0.13. A separately trained 80,786-parameter 18-step pixel DDPM and an explicit gated tracking port received the same partially occluded video inputs; held-out test: gated tracker 2 false observed joins of 567 accepted versus 40/625 ungated, with hidden-region MSE 0.006566 versus 0.007788 ungated. Fully recorded offline video replay and frozen checkpoint exist.
nodes.killed: The first zipper advantage over greedy joining is small on controlled synthetic schedules. The later Python gate is a conventional constant-velocity tracker's rejection mechanism with zipper-style reversible links, not an invocation of the original JavaScript switchyard. The tiny DDPM is not a competitive modern video diffusion architecture, its raw output hallucinates bright background, and the calibrated variant can erase real foreground. The two observed color channels make identities distinguishable when visible; natural-video object identity, truly indistinguishable objects and superior multimodal reasoning remain unproved.

edges.why: SihtiAI directly calls the Sihti signed telescoping sieve and tests a residue-informed affinity graph.
PredictiveSihtiV2 retains the exact Sihti C+R middle+R fast reconstruction in its next-frame head.
The predictor explicitly grows from the SihtiAI predictive ResidueHead prototype into coordinate-free shared local patch banks.
The constructed action witness explicitly represents hidden signed contrast as Sihti-style preserved detail.
HEAD's two-read one-specimen contrast comes from the SaturdayAfterRHproof copy-left example.
HEAD contrasts a coarse mean reading with a Sihti-like kept detail; it investigates selective access in a separate supervised training task.
The controlled identical-address/different-future witness motivates the local collision B score.
The delayed archive builds from predictive transition memory, and the webcam edition uses the real spatial Sihti head.
Sign-invariant historical relevance was inspired by HEAD's unsigned feedback, but retrospective mining uses non-gradient contingency and validation.
Saved history is asked to resolve a previously indistinguishable pair of predictive futures.
The core organizing mechanism is that discarded signed residue remains available for future retrieval.

Saved original signals and explicit reversible link archives echo Sihti's commitment to not destroying discarded distinction; the zipper is a new association operator, not a port of the diffusion sieve.
HEAD investigates selective reading; SihtiZipper explores local reversible links and abortable access without writing into other heads' original vector tracks.

PredictiveSihti's local disagreement and learned historical patches motivated a switchyard that can explicitly jam and detach incompatible streams; present zipper tension is not the predictive B variance.

motifs.title: What was unnecessary now may be essential later
motifs.description: Sihti saves signed leftovers; PredictiveSihtiV2 detects conflicts among recalled futures; LazyRetrospectiveCreditAssignment mines past residues for candidate repairs. This is synthetic evidence plus a real-world negative control, not a proven general future-cause learner.

motifs.title: A collision can choose which wire to read
motifs.description: SaturdayAfterRHproof's action-conditioned sign bit, HEAD's access experiment and PredictiveSihtiV2's B-gated motion routing ask related but different questions. HEAD's supervised gradients are not inherited by the gradient-free associative heads.

motifs.title: Smaller B can hide a worse model
motifs.description: Two null synthetic latches appeared to suppress recalled variance while making held-out forecasts worse. In real webcam footage the predictor lost to hold-last and the retrospective probe correctly declined unconfirmed associations.

motifs.title: Preserved detail still needs a trustworthy link
motifs.description: The zipper branch separates reversible binding from prediction. Explicit link gates resist wrong observations in a synthetic occluded-video task but cost coverage; a separate tiny trained diffusion denoiser has different pixel reconstruction failure modes. No demonstrated dominance over mature trackers or diffusion architectures.
